subject: Re: Luminate Health - intermittent throughput variability impacting gen endpoint
messages:
From: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@luminatehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: support@luminatehealth.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent throughput drop impacting /v1/gen - urgent

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing periodic throughput drops on our gen endpoint around 10:15–10:30 PT today. Requests that normally sit at ~1.8k reqs/min dropped to ~300 reqs/min for ~10 minutes and recovered. Latency rose (p95 from 220ms to 1.2s) and a few customer requests hit timeouts. Attached is a snapshot from our side and a short log sample.

This is affecting a production customer (live clinical summarization flows). Can you confirm whether this looks like something on Redwood's side (routing/serve/backpressure) or if there are config changes we should apply on our end? We need an ETA and a short customer-friendly explanation for the CTO.

Thanks,
Sarah
Product Ops, Luminate Health

Attachments: luminate_sample_1127.log (text)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@luminatehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent throughput drop impacting /v1/gen - urgent

Team — Sarah pinged us about a ~10-minute throughput collapse on their gen route earlier today. Luminate is in production and this is customer-impacting.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa / Evelyn: can you triage whether this was a serving/runtime event (KV eviction, kernel scheduling, burst scheduler) vs a routing/backpressure action? Share any short logs/snapshots.
- Ben / Jonas: if this is capacity/route-config related, propose a short-lived mitigation (route-level burst increase or temporary model pin) we can flip today.
- I'll draft the customer-facing note once we have the cause and the rollback plan.

CCing Sarah so they're aware we're on it. Please reply with confirmation of ownership and ETA.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent throughput drop impacting /v1/gen - urgent

Ownership: SRE taking lead. Initial triage (12:00–12:03 PT):
- Observed p95 spike and request drop correlating with a burst of requests with unusually long sequence lengths (~10–15k tokens) on the same route.
- KV-cache eviction metrics show increased churn at 10:14 PT (cache hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 58% for ~8 min). We also saw an uptick in cross-host KV fetches.
- Serving nodes reported transient CPU steal on a small subset (<8%) of the pool; we're investigating whether this caused slower kernel execution and yielded backlog.

Hypothesis: sudden shift in request characteristics (longer sequences) caused KV churn + local scheduling contention -> backlog and effective throughput drop. Not seeing obvious routing-layer overload or rate-limiter tripping.

Immediate mitigations we can enact in parallel (low-risk):
1) Enable route-specific burst capacity +1 for Luminate's gen route for 30m (will raise concurrency headroom).
2) Pin the model variant for that route to a quantized variant with slightly lower memory pressure for 1 hour (quick rollback available).
3) Enable aggressive KV-prefetch for that route (reduces cross-host fetches).

I attached a small perf snapshot and the canary logs we pulled.

Attachments: s3_perf_snapshot_2026-11-05.txt, canary-config-logs.tar.gz

If Ben can provide the exact API/config toggle, we can coordinate the change at :30. Need product/roadmap note: longer term we should have per-route sequence-length-aware autoscaling and more adaptive KV foot-printing. Jonas — can you capture this as a roadmap ask?

- Marissa
Lead SRE

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent throughput drop impacting /v1/gen - urgent

Confirmed — we can push a route-level burst increment now and pre-pin model. Quick commands (ops-only, low-risk):
- To increase burst: POST /admin/routes/{route_id}/scale {"burst_delta": 1, "duration_min": 30} -> route_id: routes/luminate-gen-prod
- To pin model: POST /admin/routes/{route_id}/pin {"model_id": "redwood/quant-v2-small"} -> will be active within ~90s and can be unpinned with the same call.

Rollback plan: unpin model and set burst_delta: -1 if we see any correctness regressions (we have canary telemetry enabled). If KV-prefetch causes elevated cross-host bandwidth, revert.

Suggested small product ask (for marketing/product): add a per-route 'sequence-length policy' flag (route.policy.sequence_threshold) that triggers temporary autoscale and kv-prefetch automatically — would prevent manual flips for customers like Luminate. Jonas, can you scope? I'd label as infra/serving backlog.

I'll make the ops calls at 13:30 PT if no objections. Evelyn — can you watch post-change telemetry (p95, throughput, kv-hit) and confirm recovery window?

- Ben
Senior Infra Engineer

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@luminatehealth.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@luminatehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: [Draft] Short customer note on earlier throughput variability — Luminate Health

Hi Sarah / Ethan —

Thanks for flagging this. Below is a short note we plan to send to affected internal stakeholders at Luminate. Please let me know if you'd like any changes before we send.

--- DRAFT ---
Summary: Between 10:14–10:24 PT on Nov 5, your gen endpoint experienced an intermittent throughput drop and elevated p95. Our on-call SREs traced the issue to a transient increase in request sequence lengths which caused higher KV cache churn and localized execution contention on a small subset of serving hosts. That combination temporarily reduced effective throughput for ~8–10 minutes.

What we did:
- Immediately increased route burst capacity and pinned the route to a lower-memory model variant to reduce memory pressure and speed execution.
- Enabled aggressive KV-prefetch for the affected route to reduce cross-host fetches.
- Monitored canaries; the route recovered within ~4 minutes after the changes and remained stable.

Next steps (short term):
- SRE will continue to monitor the route closely for 48 hours; we'll share a short follow-up with telemetry.
- Product will capture a feature request to add sequence-length-aware autoscaling and per-route KV policies to avoid manual interventions for similar events.

What you should do (recommended):
- No action needed on your side for now. If you anticipate a sustained increase in long-sequence requests, let us know and we can advise on model choice and routing configuration proactively.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate you bringing this to our attention.

If this draft looks good, we'll send from the SRE/Aditya channel to Luminate and include the CTO update.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
---

Aditya (sending when team confirms recovery metrics)
